a:r.a:t: Another Rift-exclusive feature is stateful testing with flow state.
Mountebank is stateless by design - each request is independent. But real systems have state. Retry logic, rate limiting, circuit breakers - these all depend on previous requests.

Rift adds a flow state store that persists across requests. You can use it with three scripting engines: JavaScript for Mountebank compatibility, Rhai which is a Rust-native scripting language, or Lua.
This example uses Rhai to implement retry testing. It increments a counter for each request. If it's request 1 or 2, return a 503 error. On request 3 or later, let the normal response through.
This lets you test that your application correctly retries failed requests - without spinning up a real failing service.
For distributed testing, you can back the flow state with Redis instead of in-memory storage.
